title: Last Glacial Maximum
summary: The Last Glacial Maximum marked the peak extent of continental ice sheets during the final glacial cycle, lowering global sea level by approximately 130 meters and locking vast water volumes into the Laurentide, Fennoscandian, and Antarctic ice sheets. This profound cold interval reshaped global vegetation into extensive steppe-tundra, exposed continental shelves including the Bering Land Bridge, and closed interior migration corridors into North America, channeling and isolating human populations across northern Eurasia and Beringia.

importance.justification: The Last Glacial Maximum represents the peak of global ice sheet extent during the last glacial cycle, dramatically lowering sea levels and shaping planetary climate and human migration corridors.
